changes.reason: The Chain editor now formats visible range guidance separately while retaining the exact Task Definition bounds for validation and HTML input attributes.
The new formatter rounds the lower bound upward and upper bound downward at display precision, with an exact-bound fallback for intervals narrower than one display step.
The unit evidence fixes raw-float suppression, inward rounding, and the narrow-interval fallback without changing the domain contract.
The browser evidence confirms that exact raw bounds remain on the input while visible guidance follows the declared display precision.

claim_assessments.statement: Task Definition allowed_range remains the exact validation and input-attribute boundary, while display_decimals controls only reader-facing range presentation.
claim_assessments.reason: Without this distinction, a learner could treat a rounded label as a changed scientific domain or reproduce binary floating-point noise in the interface.

evidence.symbol: allowed range rounds inward so a displayed bound is never rejected on entry
Chain candidate editor exposes and persists every external input from its contract
